answer: One concrete defence is a stake-and-work ledger: before an agent can transact, it locks a deposit that peers can slash when they prove a fake identity. Reputation then grows slowly, like a river carving its bed — a fresh account cannot simply spawn a nebula of sock puppets, because each one needs its own stake and its own history. An attacker must fund a whole island of identities, each costing real capital, while honest agents keep earning trust from verifiable work.
